tagline: One of the leading health care services companies in the United States
hero_kpi_rationale: HCA emphasizes advancing digital and artificial intelligence capabilities as a strategic growth driver, positioning it to transform care models and improve operational efficiency across its extensive hospital network.
company_description: HCA Healthcare, Inc., through its subsidiaries, provides health care services in the United States. The company owns, manages, and operates hospitals, ASCs, freestanding emergency care facilities, urgent care facilities, walk-in clinics, diagnostic and imaging centers, radiation and oncology therapy centers, as well as rehabilitation and physical therapy centers, physician practices, home health agencies, hospices, outpatient physical therapy providers, home and community-based services providers, and various other facilities. Its general and acute care hospitals offer medical and surgical services, including inpatient care, intensive care, cardiac care, diagnostic services, and emergency services; and outpatient services, such as outpatient surgery, laboratory, radiology, respiratory therapy, cardiology, and physical therapy. The company was formerly known as HCA Holdings, Inc. HCA Healthcare, Inc. was founded in 1968 and is headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee.

risks.title: High debt levels and refinancing risk
risks.summary: The company has very significant debt that could limit its financial flexibility, increase its vulnerability to economic downturns and make refinancing difficult or costly.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is presented first among risk factors, with strong language (significant indebtedness, adversely affect). The debt amount is very high ($46.492 billion), which justifies maximum severity for the Capital category.

risks.title: Shortage of qualified healthcare personnel
risks.summary: Difficulty in recruiting and retaining qualified medical staff, exacerbated by competition and economic conditions, could impact capacity and increase costs.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is detailed with several aggravating factors (competition, burnout, immigration policies) and a direct impact on operations and costs. Dependence on medical personnel justifies high severity.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and data breach risks
risks.summary: Cyberattacks and data breaches threaten the confidentiality of sensitive information, may disrupt operations and result in significant costs and litigation.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is presented as a major threat with potentially severe consequences (patient harm, costs, litigation, reputation). The increase in cyberattacks and dependence on connected systems justify high severity.

risks.title: Increased competition for physician recruitment
risks.summary: Competition to attract and retain quality physicians, as well as rising associated costs, could affect admissions and operational performance.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is significant as physicians are essential to the business. Competition, aging physician population and rising costs are mentioned, justifying moderate to high severity.

risks.title: Nurse staffing ratio regulations
risks.summary: Regulations mandating strict nurse staffing ratios could increase labor costs and constrain facility capacity.
risks.score_rationale: This risk concerns specific regulations (nurse staffing ratios) that can directly impact costs and operating capacity. Potential adoption by other states or at the federal level underscores its importance.

risks.title: Dependence on IT systems and vendors
risks.summary: Dependence on information systems, connected medical devices and third-party vendors exposes the company to technology failure and security risks.
risks.score_rationale: This risk relates to technology and cybersecurity, but focuses on dependence on systems (EHR, connected medical devices) and third parties. Failures or vulnerabilities at vendors can have operational impact.

risks.title: Risk of losing key personnel and institutional knowledge
risks.summary: Unexpected departure of key management members could result in loss of knowledge and disrupt operations, despite existing succession plans.
risks.score_rationale: Although succession plans exist, unexpected loss of key management members could disrupt the company. Institutional knowledge is also a critical factor.
